en: The Sutra of the Great Sovereign Dhāraṇī Divine Mantra of the Spontaneous Attainment of All Desires, as Spoken by the Buddha;
Translated during the Great Tang Dynasty by [the Master from] Kaśmīra in North India.
Translated at the Tianguan Monastery by the Tripiṭaka Master Ratnākarasiṃha: Thus have I heard.
At one time, the Bhagavat was staying at Mount Gṛdhrakūṭa in the great city of Rājagṛha.
While he was teaching the Dharma together with his disciples,
Mahābrahmā, the lord of the Sahā world, came to where the Buddha was,
circumambulated him three times to the right, and stood before him.
Prostrating at the Buddha's feet and joining his palms toward the Buddha,
he addressed the Buddha, saying: "I only pray, World-Honored One,
that for the sake of benefiting sentient beings..."
He spoke this dhāraṇī mantra,
causing all humans and devas to universally attain peace and happiness.
The Buddha said, "Excellent, excellent, Great Brahmā King!"
"You are able to take pity on all sentient beings and ask about this matter of benefit.
Reflect upon it well; I shall analyze and explain it for you."
This is the Great Sovereign Dhāraṇī Mantra of the Wish-Fulfilling [Amoghapāśa],
which can bestow the most supreme peace and happiness upon all sentient beings,
and protect them from all yakṣas and rākṣasas.
Furthermore, they shall not be afflicted by epilepsy, hungry ghosts (*preta*),
*kumbhāṇḍa* spirits, or various other malevolent spirits;
nor shall they be harmed or impaired by diseases such as cold or heat.
Wherever one dwells, one will always achieve victory; one will not be harmed by combatants or enemies, but will be able to crush opposing forces.
Malevolent incantations, curses, and spells shall be unable to cause harm.
All the karmic offenses of past lives will be completely extinguished;
poison cannot harm, fire cannot burn,
blades cannot wound, and water cannot drown them.
They shall not be harmed by thunder, lightning, or untimely winds and torrential rains.
If there are those who receive and uphold this divine mantra,
they shall attain victory wherever they go.
If one can write this down and wear it around the neck or on the arm,
that person will be able to accomplish all virtuous deeds with supreme purity and will be constantly protected by the devas and nāga kings.
Furthermore, they are remembered by all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas,
as well as by Vajrapāṇi, the Four Great Heavenly Kings, Śakra Devendra, and Mahābrahmā.
Viṣṇu, Maheśvara, Kumāra, the hosts of the army, the Piśācas, Mahākāla, Nandikeśvara, and the like.
Day and night, they shall constantly follow and protect those who uphold this mantra.
Furthermore, the host of Māṭikaṇṭha devas and other hosts of sovereign celestial deities shall likewise provide protection.
Furthermore, for the sake of the various māra-deva hosts and their retinues of spirit-mantra deities of great majestic power—
namely, the deity Aṅkuśī and the deity Vajrapāṇi— [he spoke].
The deity Śaṅkara, the deity Māmakī, the deity Bhṛkuṭī, the deity Tārā,
the deity Mahākāla, and the deity Dūtī.
The deity Kṣakārapaṇi, the deity Mahābala,
the deity Dīrghāyus, the deity Mahādevī,
the deity Kārakaṇi, and the deity Puṣpadanta.
The deity Maṇicūḍā, the deity Suvarṇacūḍā,
the deity Piṅgala, the deity Bhāṇḍa, the deity Vidyutprabhā,
the deity Karālī, and the deity Vikuñcī.
The Earth Goddess Dṛḍhā; the Goddess Udakadattā;
the God Śvetaśaila; the Greatly Wrathful God;
the Sword-Wielding God; and the Jewel-Radiance God.
The deity Śāṇḍilya, the deity Śāṭha,
the deity Buddhadaṇḍapālinī, the deity Laṅkeśvara,
and countless other celestial deities.
All those hosts of devas will come to protect him.
If this divine mantra is held in one's hands or body,
the spirit Maṇibhadra, the father and mother of the Kumbhāṇḍas, [will likewise provide protection].
The goddesses Pūrṇabhadra and Mahābala,
the goddess Jayantī and the goddess Kūṭadanti,
as well as Śrīdevī, Mahāprajñādevī, and others.
They shall constantly follow and protect her.
If there is a woman who upholds this divine mantra,
she will possess great power and shall always give birth to sons.
When one receives and maintains [this practice], one will be secure while in the womb;
the birth will be peaceful and free from all illness;
and all transgressions will be extinguished—of this there is no doubt.
By the power of their merit, their wealth and grain increase;
the teachings they proclaim are accepted with faith by all people,
and they are constantly honored and served by everyone.
Whether they be men or women, boys or girls,
those who maintain this dhāraṇī should purify themselves;
they shall obtain peace and happiness, be free from all diseases, and their physical appearance shall be radiant and flourishing.
May auspicious merit and virtue increase to perfection;
may all dhāraṇī practices attain accomplishment.
Even one who wears this mantra has not yet entered the maṇḍala.
One immediately achieves entry into all maṇḍalas;
one's conduct becomes identical to that of those who have entered the maṇḍala;
and evil dreams and grave transgressions are extinguished.
Should anyone with an evil mind approach them,
they will be unable to cause harm to those who maintain this mantra.
All their desires and whatever they seek shall be attained.
